thread_title: S. minor var. minor Brooks Co, GA
breadcrumb: S. minor var. minor Brooks Co, GA

posts.body_html:
Here are some interesting genotypes of S. minor var. minor that originate from a large site (on private property) in Brooks Co, GA. The site is reportedly housing one of the largest flava var. rugelii population in the entire state of Georgia!

I think these plants are somewhat new to cultivation, and from what I can tell, they're not yet circulating in collections just yet. I don't really know much about these plants just yet, as they are still babies, but I do know that divisions were made, so they're now available.

S. minor var. minor Brooks Co, GA, pics taken 10/1/22:


here's a clone with some nice girth to it!

I think these plants are somewhat new to cultivation, and from what I can tell, they're not yet circulating in collections just yet.  I don't really know much about these plants just yet, as they are still babies, but I do know that divisions were made, so they're now available.

posts.body_html: Glad to see these in cultivation! I've been to the property and you could get lost in fields of flavas. Lots of x harperi. Years ago the new owners were still removing thick brush and burning, so you could see flava pushing up all over! It must be nice to see now. They grow with Drosera tracyi too - one of only a couple sites left in GA.
